title: 'Uber won': Why Instacart might not stand a chance
content:
Uber (UBER) and Maplebear (CART) (Instacart's parent company) both reported quarterly earnings on Wednesday.

BNP Paribas US large-cap internet equity analyst Nick Jones joins Yahoo Finance's Josh Lipton to discuss the key differences between the two companies and why he thinks Uber has much more room to run.

Video Transcript

00:00 Speaker A

What makes Uber different, Nick than the competition? What what's their competitive edge and advantage?

00:09 Nick

The competitive advantage is Uber one. Um you probably know more and more people who have the subscription and the platform, the kind of the flywheel we see here is you can combine mobility with delivery. So not only can you take a cab or a robotaxi service or a taxi service somewhere, you can also use it to order food uh at a hotel or to your home and you can increasingly use it for grocery and other retail items. So, they're really creating this kind of on demand commerce platform that really leverages their mobility footprint. So, um that is a very powerful flywheel when you compare to maybe um Instacart which is really focused on grocery does a little bit of food delivery. Um and similar to kind of door dash, which is really focused on meal delivery and increasingly grocery as well. So, they really have a lot of revenue streams tied to their platform and the subscription offering. So that's all, it's a lot of value there for the users.

01:13 Speaker A

In our robo taxi future, Nick, is Uber a winner or a victim?

01:22 Nick

We think it's a winner. We think it's a winner. This is one of the hottest debates when we talk to investors. Um ultimately, we believe selection is going to matter. What is really going to steer consumers? It's going to be pricing and convenience, or in other words, can I get a taxi service quickly? Or do I have to wait? So, ultimately, we think uh autonomous vehicles will be fragmented in the end. Selection and convenience are going to matter and Uber's got the most powerful distribution network.

01:46 Speaker A

I know you like Uber, Nick, got an outperform, right? So you're telling clients this one's a buy. What are the catalysts ahead, Nick, that you say, hey, it's going to keep moving this one higher?

01:58 Nick

I think we see a lot of partnership with Zeus, Nero, they have an Nvidia partnership. So as they start launching robot taxis across their platform this year, they're planning to get to 15 cities by the end of the year and many more after that. So once we get to see um these autonomous vehicles deployed on the platform and really get a a first hand look at the economics and the competitive landscape against Waymo and Tesla and other players. I think that will act as someone of a clearing event and help build confidence in kind of the trajectory Uber's developed so far are um year to day.

02:40 Speaker A

Let's talk about Instacart, Nick, because they reported. Investors not as excited about that one. What do you make of that print? What happened here?

02:51 Nick

Orders came in lighter than expected. Um so while they've delivered pretty strong revenue results and guidance was pretty good as well, the underlying kind of KPIs are how many how many orders are there and how much does each order cost? And orders came in lighter than expected, which suggests there may be some issues with uh uh the upper funnel and attracting more and more customers. And they even guided to that on the call that order growth um is likely to track with customer growth from here. And with third-party data, we see some stagnation in user growth. So I think investors are sniffing out while the kind of headline numbers look pretty good, some of the core inputs to durable growth uh may uh show some cracks right now, which is part of the reason we have an underperformed rating.

03:32 Speaker A

Customers are shifting to cheaper retailers. So I guess they're they're looking for value, they're looking for deals. How does that impact InstaCart in terms of, you know, take rate, profitability, Nick.

03:45 Nick

They probably divert consumers to platforms like Amazon, um potentially Walmart or other uh kind of more cost-effective channels. And people are often kind of weighing the deal versus the convenience and Amazon's the behemoth when it comes to cheap prices and very convenient experience because they can deliver, you know, same day next day for a large swath of kind of consumer staple type items.

title: After a long gap, Uber Freight’s revenue turns higher from year earlier
content:
Uber Freight reported its financial performance on the basis of operating income rather than EBITDA for the first time, but the negative numbers came as revenue turned up after a long stretch of lower numbers.

The operating loss for the first quarter at the company known primarily as a digital broker was $30 million. While this quarter was the first time where Uber’s three segments–Mobility, Delivery and Freight–were reported on the basis of operating income rather than EBITDA, the company’s earnings statement did report operating income at Uber Freight for the first quarter of 2025 as a loss of $25 million.

In the company’s supplemental information released with the earnings, the operating loss for the second, third and fourth quarters of last year at Uber Freight was $26 million, $40 million and $18 million, respectively.

When Uber Freight (NYSE: UBER) reported income on an EBITDA basis, it only squeaked out a positive number in the third and fourth quarters of 2022, and was breakeven on an EBITDA basis in the fourth quarter of last year. Otherwise, it was negative each quarter since its inception.

But revenue rose to $1.34 billion from $1.26 billion a year ago. Freight revenue in the fourth quarter was $1.27 billion.

Not since the third quarter of 2024 could Uber Freight do a year-on-year quarterly comparison and see revenue more than what it was four quarters earlier. Between the third quarter of 2023 and 3Q 2024, Uber Freight eked out a gain in revenue of $25 million.

But in the first quarter of 2026, the year-on-year revenue gain was $47 million.

In a post on LinkedIn, Uber Freight CEO Rebecca Tinucci was upbeat about Uber Freight’s prospects, noting that the year-on-year increase in revenue was the first for the group in two years. (Uber DEO Dara Khosrowshahi, who rarely mentions Uber Freight in the company’s earnings calls with analysts, also cited the revenue increase in this quarter’s session).

“At a high level, Freight delivered strong topline performance, driven by continued strength in enterprise demand and Managed Transportation — even as the market tightened in ways we haven’t seen in some time,” Tinucci said. “The team continued to lean in with customers through the tightening — maintaining service while others pulled back.”

Story Continues

Tinucci added that new enterprise customers came with about $165 million in “new addressable spend.” That figure was roughly equal to all new customer spend from 2025, Tinucci said.

The Managed Transportation group at Uber Freight has its roots in the legacy Transplace acquisition from 2021. Transplace is known primarily as a provider of transportation management systems to shippers.

Tinucci said Uber Freight has been seeing “a more unified approach across the business — bringing together Managed Transportation and brokerage in a way that’s driving growth across both and reinforcing the value of a more integrated model for enterprise customers.”

title: Uber Technologies, Inc. Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Uber Technologies, Inc. Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance and Operational Drivers

Performance exceeded guidance driven by trip-led growth and a 17% increase in audience engagement across Mobility and Delivery. Mobility gross bookings accelerated to 20% growth, supported by record margins and a recovery in the Freight segment. Strategic focus on 'Uber One' loyalty has reached 50 million members, with members spending 3x more than non-members and exhibiting higher retention. The 'GO-GET' initiative is transitioning Uber from an on-demand service to a planned travel platform, exemplified by the expansion into hotel bookings via Expedia. Autonomous vehicle (AV) trips grew 10x year-over-year, supported by a hybrid network strategy involving over 30 global partners. Management attributes margin expansion to disciplined cost management and operating leverage, with EPS growing twice as fast as bookings.

Growth Outlook and Strategic Initiatives

Guidance assumes continued momentum in U.S. Mobility acceleration throughout 2026, driven by favorable insurance rate renewals and price elasticity. The company plans to be live with autonomous vehicle deployments in up to 15 cities by the end of 2024, with significant scaling expected in 2025. Management is pivoting toward AI-driven efficiency, expecting increased infrastructure investment to be offset by slower headcount growth. Strategic expansion into 'sparse markets' (suburbs) is a key growth lever, as these areas are currently growing 2x faster than core urban markets. Future scaling of AVs depends on building a capital-light ecosystem including third-party financing, specialized insurance, and fleet management partnerships.

Operational Context and Risk Factors

Insurance cost savings in the U.S. are expected to reach hundreds of millions of dollars in 2026, marking the first year of significant leverage since COVID. The launch of 'Uber Autonomous Solutions' represents a strategic shift toward providing technical and operational infrastructure for AV partners. Management noted that while AI tools are increasing developer throughput, they initially underestimated the required investment levels in late 2025. A record $3 billion was returned to shareholders via buybacks this quarter, reflecting a commitment to disciplined capital allocation.

Q&A Session Highlights

Insurance cost savings and U.S. Mobility acceleration

Management expects hundreds of millions in savings due to improved policy work and favorable auto insurance market renewals in March. Savings are being reinvested into consumer pricing to drive trip growth, particularly in California where L.A. is outperforming the rest of the country.

Story Continues

AI's role in cross-platform usage and personalization

AI is being used to move away from fixed user interfaces toward personalized 'agentic' experiences like 'Cart Assistant' and predictive destination cards. Currently, 75% of Mobility destinations are successfully predicted by AI, and $15 billion in Delivery bookings now originate from the Mobility app.

Competitive dynamics in international Delivery markets

Uber is taking an 'offensive footing' in Europe against competitors like DoorDash and Prosus, recently launching in Finland. In APAC, sparse market expansion has reaccelerated the Australian business to 30% growth despite high existing penetration.

Risk of user abstraction by third-party AI agents

Management dismissed fears of being 'abstracted away' by Meta or Google agents, citing their direct relationship with 50 million Uber One members. Dara Khosrowshahi compared the situation to travel metasearch, noting that value typically accrues to the large, consolidated service providers with the best core products.

title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 at Record Highs on Tech Earnings and US-Iran Peace Hopes
content:
The S&P 500 Index ($SPX) (SPY) today is up +1.19%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DOWI) (DIA) is up +1.33%, and the Nasdaq 100 Index ($IUXX) (QQQ) is up +1.44%.  June E-mini S&P futures (ESM26) are up +1.19%, and June E-mini Nasdaq futures (NQM26) are up +1.47%.

Stock indexes are soaring today, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 posting new all-time highs.  A wave of blockbuster earnings results from chipmakers and AI-infrastructure stocks are propelling stocks higher today and has bolstered optimism that the relentless pace of investment in artificial intelligence will continue.  Advanced Micro Devices is up more than +16% after data center spending boosted its full-year sales forecast, and Super Micro Computer is up more than +17% after reporting improved margins and giving a solid profit forecast. Join 200K+ Subscribers: Find out why the midday Barchart Brief newsletter is a must-read for thousands daily.

Stocks extended their gains as crude oil prices plunged and bond yields tumbled on optimism that the US and Iran are nearing a peace deal.  The US believes it's close to an agreement with Iran to end the war, and President Trump suspended a military initiative to guide stranded ships through the Strait of Hormuz and said, "Great progress has been made toward a complete and final agreement with representatives of Iran."  He added that a US blockade of ships transiting to and from Iranian ports would "remain in full force and effect" until a deal is agreed to.  Crude prices sank to a 2-week low, and the 10-year T-note yield fell to a 1-week low of 4.33%

Axios reported today that the US and Iran are working on a one-page memorandum of understanding that, if Iran accepts it, will lead to the gradual reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the lifting of the US blockade on Iranian ports.  Nothing has yet been agreed upon, and detailed negotiations on Iran’s nuclear program will come later in the process.  Also, China's top diplomat, Foreign Minister Wang Yi, called for the swift reopening of the Strait of Hormuz during a meeting with his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Arachchi, in Beijing today.

Stocks maintained their gains on the Fed-friendly Apr ADP employment change report that showed US companies added 109,000 jobs, below expectations of 120,000.

Comments today from St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem were hawkish and negative for stocks when he said, "Inflation is running meaningfully above our 2% target.  We have risks on the employment side and on the inflation side, and in my understanding, the risks have been shifting towards more risk on the inflation side than the employment side."

WTI crude oil prices (CLM26) plummeted more than -6% today to a 2-week low after Axios reported that the US believes it’s close to an agreement with Iran to end the nearly 10-week war.  The US sees Iran responding within 48 hours to a one-page memorandum of understanding to end the war, which would include both sides lifting restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz.  The strait remains essentially closed, as about a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas transits through the strait.  Goldman Sachs estimates that the current disruption has drawn down nearly 500 million bbl from global crude stockpiles, with the drawdown potentially reaching 1 billion bbl by June.

The markets are discounting a 6% chance of a -25 bp FOMC rate cut at the next FOMC meeting on June 16-17.

Earnings results thus far this reporting season have been supportive of stocks.  As of today, 84% of the 375 S&P 500 companies that reported Q1 earnings have beaten estimates.  Q1 S&P 500 earnings are projected to climb +12% y/y, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.  Stripping out the technology sector, Q1 earnings are projected to increase around +3%, the weakest in two years.

Overseas stock markets are higher today.  The Euro Stoxx 50 climbed to a 2.5-week high and is up sharply by +2.46%.  China's Shanghai Composite rallied to a 2-month high and closed up +1.17%.  Japan's Nikkei Stock Average did not trade, with markets in Japan closed for a National holiday.

Interest Rates

June 10-year T-notes (ZNM6) today are up by +13 ticks.  The 10-year T-note yield is down -6.8 bp to 4.356%.  Jun T-notes rallied to a 1-week high today, and the 10-year T-note yield fell to a 1-week low of 4.331%.  T-notes are climbing today on the heels of a -6% plunge in crude oil prices to a 2-week low, which eases inflation expectations.  The 10-year breakeven inflation rate fell to a 1-week low of 2.417% today.  T-notes maintained their gains after the Apr ADP employment change came in below expectations, a dovish factor for Fed policy.

The US Treasury today said it will keep its quarterly refunding sales of government debt unchanged from last quarter at $125 billion and said it sees coupon issuance steady "at least the next several quarters.

European government bond yields are moving lower today.  The 10-year German Bund yield fell to a 2-week low of 2.963% and is down -7.1 bp to 2.992%.  The 10-year UK gilt yield fell to a 1.5-week low of 4.905% and is down -12.4 bp to 4.937%.

Eurozone Mar PPI rose +2.1% y/y, stronger than expectations of 1.8% y/y and the fastest pace of increase in a year.

The Eurozone Apr S&P composite PMI was revised upward by +0.2 to 48.8 from the previously reported 48.6.

Swaps are discounting a 77% chance of a +25 bp ECB rate hike at its next policy meeting on June 11.

US Stock Movers

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is up more than +15% to lead gainers in the Nasdaq 100 and lead chip makers and AI-infrastructure stocks higher after reporting Q1 revenue of $10.25 billion, better than the consensus of $9.89 billion, and forecasting Q2 revenue of $10.90 billion to $11.50 billion, well above the consensus of $10.52 billion.  Super Micro Computer (SMCI) is up more than +17% to lead gainers in the S&P 500 after forecasting Q4 net sales of $11.0 billion to $12.5 billion, the midpoint well above the consensus of $11.16 billion.  Also, ARM Holdings Plc (ARM) is up more than +9%, and Lam Research (LRCX) is up more than +7%. In addition, ASML Holding NV (ASML) is up more than +5%, and Nvidia (NVDA) is up more than +4%. Finally, Applied Materials (AMAT) and KLA Corp (KLAC) are up more than +3%, and Micron Technology (MU), Intel (INTC), and Texas Instruments (TXN) are up more than +2%.

Airline stocks and cruise line operators are climbing today, with WTI crude oil sinking more than -6% to a 2-week low, which lowers fuel costs and boosts the profitability prospects for the companies.  United Airlines Holdings (UAL), Alaska Air Group (ALK), and Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd (RCL) are up more than +5%, and American Airlines Group (AAL), Carnival (CCL), and Southwest Airlines (LUV) are up more than +4%.  In addition, Delta Air Lines (DAL) is up more than +4%, and Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings (NCLH) is up more than +1%.

Mining stocks are rallying today with gold, silver, and copper prices surging.  Coeur Mining (CDE) is up more than +9%, and Hecla Mining (HL) is up more than +8%. Also, Anglogold Ashanti (AU) and Barrick Mining (B) are up more than 7%, and Southern Copper (SCCO), Newmont Corp (NEM), and Freeport McMoRan (FCX) are up more than +5%.

Energy producers and service providers are retreating today, with crude oil prices tumbling more than -6% to a 2-week low.  Devon Energy (DVN), APA Corp (APA), and Occidental Petroleum (OXY) are down more than -6%, and Valero Energy (VLO) is down more than -5%.  Also, Diamondback Energy (FANG), Phillips 66 (PSX), and Marathon Petroleum (MPC) are down more than -4%, and Chevron (CVX) is down more than -4% to lead losers in the Dow Jones Industrials.  In addition, ConocoPhillips (COP) and Exxon Mobil (XOM) are down more than -3%, and Halliburton (HAL) is down more than -2%.

Flex Ltd (FLEX) is up more than +30% after reporting Q4 net sales of $7.48 billion, better than the consensus of $6.94 billion, and forecasting 2027 revenue of $32.3 billion to $33.8 billion, well above the consensus of $29.15 billion.

DaVita (DVA) is up more than +20% after reporting Q1 total revenue of $3.42 billion, better than the consensus of $3.34 billion and forecasting full-year adjusted EPS continuing operations of $14.10 to $15.20, the midpoint well above the consensus of $14.11.

Uber Technologies (UBER) is up more than +8% after reporting Q2 gross bookings of $53.72 billion, above the consensus of $52.92 billion.

Walt Disney (DIS) is up more than +7% to lead gainers in the Dow Jones Industrials after reporting Q2 revenue of $25.17 billion, above the consensus of $24.87 billion.

CVS Health (CVS) is up more than +7% after raising its full-year adjusted EPS forecast to $7.30 to $7.50 from a prior forecast of $7.00 to $7.20, stronger than the consensus of $7.12.

Oscar Health (OSCR) is up more than +4% after reporting Q1 adjusted Ebitda of $727.1 million, well above the consensus of $435.7 million.

Primoris Services (PRIM) is down more than -44% after reporting Q1 revenue of $1.56 billion, well below the consensus of $1.73 billion.

CDW Corp (CDW) is down more than -22% to lead losers in the S&P 500 after reporting Q1 adjusted EPS of $2.28, weaker than the consensus of $2.30.

TransMedics Group (TMDX) is down more than -21% after reporting Q1 adjusted diluted earnings per share of 30 cents, well below the consensus of 59 cents.

Cencora (COR) is down more than -15% after reporting Q2 revenue of $78.36 billion, well below the consensus of $81.01 billion.

Coupang (CPNG) is down more than -15% after reporting a Q1 gross profit margin of 27%, below the consensus of 27.9%.
